narrative:
The model predicted a 67% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the strongest influences pushing the prediction toward failure. Both placed you in the bottom decile of your school, far below the average of roughly sixth decile among students who were accepted. These consistently low academic standings signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Your LSAT score worked in the opposite direction, modestly pulling the prediction toward passing. At 36 it sits only slightly below the 37.2 average of accepted students, giving the model some reassurance about your potential.

Your undergraduate GPA of 2.5, while below the 3.23 average of accepted applicants, and your lower-middle family income (which is uncommon among accepted students) played smaller supporting roles but were not the main drivers.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance and consider retaking the LSAT to boost that score. Strengthening these areas will directly address the factors that most influenced this outcome. (218 words)
